input.reasoning_summary:
After reconsidering the initial verdict in light of the critique, the label remains SUPPORTED. The claim makes a simple factual assertion: that NVIDIA's gross margin for fiscal year 2026 was lower than in fiscal year 2025. This is unambiguously confirmed by E4, which states gross margin decreased from 75.0% to 71.1%. 

All three weaknesses are supported by the evidence but do not contradict the claim itself. W1 correctly identifies that approximately 2.6 percentage points of the decrease was due to one-time inventory charges (E6). W2 correctly notes that quarterly margins improved through the year (72.4% in Q2, 73.4% in Q3 per E3 and E5), indicating the full-year figure was weighted down by Q1. W3 correctly identifies a structural business model transition as a contributing factor (E2, E5). 

However, the claim does not state any cause for the decrease, nor does it characterize the decrease as operational vs. one-time or temporary vs. structural. It simply asserts that FY2026 gross margin was lower than FY2025, which is factually correct regardless of the underlying drivers. The weaknesses provide important context about the nature of the decrease but do not refute the core factual assertion.
